scope: Clarifies the physical size-metric evidence for the existing UDM-radius to RRTMGP-diameter coordinate conversion. No source, coefficient, default, multiplier, build, or model-run changes.

WRF/phys/module_mp_udm.F.locator: udm_mp_effective_radius; ice empirical polynomial and configured radius bounds

WRF/phys/module_ra_rrtmgp.F.locator: rrtmgp_ice_lut_coordinate; explicit radius-to-diameter conversion, with flag-3 Fu adjustment

WRF/external/rte_rrtmgp/rrtmgp-frontend/.locator: cloud_optics input comments and bounds checks; frontend comments cite Yang et al. (2013)

WRF/external/rte_rrtmgp/extensions/mo_lo.locator: loader reads diameter-named ice bounds from the LUT

WRF/external/rte_rrtmgp/DATA.json.locator: pins data repository and exact cloud coefficient files

metric_relationship.udm_attribution: The UDM polynomial's form and coefficients match Wyser Eq. (35); this is an equation-form inference. The local source credits Soo Ya Bae (2015) without an explicit Wyser citation.
metric_relationship.conditional_definition: For identical PSD, habits, volume, and orientation-averaged projected area: r_VA=3*V_total/(4*A_total), D_VA=3*V_total/(2*A_total), hence D_VA=2*r_VA.
metric_relationship.wyser_1998: Eqs. (19)-(20) define a randomly oriented column geometric proxy and cross-section-weighted population mean; Eq. (35) fits the Eq. (20) value from the paper's PSD and geometry assumptions.
metric_relationship.unresolved: The inspected primary and pinned table materials do not prove Wyser Eq. (35) radius and the pinned table diameter use the same physical metric.
metric_relationship.fu_terminology: D_VA is called volume/projected-area effective diameter here; it is not identified with Fu generalized effective size Dge.

references.citation: Wyser (1998), The Effective Radius in Ice Clouds, Journal of Climate 11, 1793-1802
references.access_note: Publisher indexed text returned equation-referencing body text; direct page/PDF access returned HTTP 403 in review environment; no local PDF or file hash.

references.citation: Wyser and Yang (1998), Average ice crystal size and bulk short-wave single-scattering properties of cirrus clouds
references.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract describes average size as total volume divided by total projected area; it does not equate this to Wyser Eq. (35).

references.citation: Yang et al. (2013), Spectrally Consistent Scattering, Absorption, and Polarization Properties of Atmospheric Ice Crystals

conclusion: The adapter's factor two is an explicit coordinate conversion from radius to diameter. These sources do not prove or disprove physical-metric equivalence for the pinned LUT. No factor-two defect or additional multiplier is established.
